selection.rationale: Objective is ttft_ms, which the adapter times over exactly the prefill forward (256 GPU-resident prompt tokens, batch 1) plus the explicit first-token-ready cudaDeviceSynchronize; decode time cannot improve the metric. Observed prefill CUDA time is 21.46 ms for Qwen3ForCausalLM, of which the 36 decoder layers hold 20.60 ms and the Qwen3MLP block alone holds 11.77 ms (57%). Inside MLP, the gate_proj/up_proj pair is 7.66 ms spread over 72 separate aten::linear GEMMs of shape (256x2560)x(2560x9728) in BF16 - many narrow-N GEMMs at modest M=256, which is the largest single coherent inefficiency on the TTFT path (SDPA is only 0.73 ms, so attention kernels are not the lever). The editable boundary is one code path: Qwen3MLP.forward together with the gate_proj/up_proj nn.Linear modules it calls; the observed module calls and their aten::linear child calls that a packed projection replaces are included. The same edited module object also runs in the 31 decode steps of the frozen 32-token completion (decode diagnostic 186.1 ms for Qwen3MLP, 121.8 ms for its gate/up linears), so its decode-phase groups are part of the boundary both to keep the frozen workload and quality gates intact (require_exact_greedy_tokens over the full completion, logits atol/rtol 0.02) and because the workload also carries the decode_tokens_per_second goal. Task is single-device (resources.json: communication not applicable), so no cross-rank effects exist. Down_proj, SiLU/mul, norms and attention are untouched and excluded.
selection.hypothesis: Replace the two per-layer gate/up projections with a single packed BF16 GEMM (weights concatenated once at model-load time from the frozen checkpoint along the output dimension, 2560->19456, then split), leaving dtype, TF32 policy, seed, real data and workload boundaries unchanged. In prefill this halves the projection kernel count (72->36 GEMMs) and gives the BF16 GEMM a wider N at M=256, which we hypothesize cuts the observed 7.66 ms prefill gate/up CUDA time by roughly 15-30% (~1.2-2.3 ms), i.e. about 5-10% of ttft_ms, with a similar per-step effect in decode as a secondary benefit. Exact greedy tokens and logits within 0.02 atol/rtol are expected to be preserved since each output element keeps the same K=2560 dot product; this is a measurable prediction to be tested with the paired ttft_ms repeats and quality checks, not an assumed benefit, and kernel-choice changes in accumulation order are the main risk to watch.

proposal.rationale: Objective is ttft_ms (paired repeats, minimize), timed by the adapter over the prefill forward of 256 GPU-resident prompt tokens plus the explicit first-token-ready cudaDeviceSynchronize; decode cannot improve the metric but the same edited modules run there, so the frozen 32-token completion and its decode_tokens_per_second goal stay on the transformed path. Observed prefill CUDA time is 21.46 ms for Qwen3ForCausalLM, with 11.77 ms in the 36 Qwen3MLP blocks; inside each MLP the gate_proj/up_proj pair costs 7.66 ms spread over 72 aten::linear GEMMs of shape (256x2560)x(2560x9728) BF16 (SDPA is only 0.73 ms, so attention is not the lever). This joint candidate replaces the forward of all 36 Qwen3MLP modules at their observed module call sites (36 prefill-phase sites + 36 decode-phase sites = the 72 call IDs in replacement_calls, selected groups bbb72243cf9b53ec7b51 and 8fc5d2f4cd28158578d8). Each replacement computes down_proj(act_fn(gate) * up) exactly as the parent does, but obtains gate/up from one packed BF16 GEMM x @ [Wg; Wu]^T with the [19456, 2560] weight concatenated once at build time from the frozen checkpoint weights, then splits along the output dimension (gate = proj[..., :9728], up = proj[..., 9728:]). In prefill this halves the projection kernel count (72 -> 36 GEMMs) and widens N from 9728 to 19456 at M=256, improving tensor-core tile occupancy on the dominant TTFT path; in decode (M=1) it halves the per-MLP launch count while reading the same weight bytes, a small secondary benefit. Every output element keeps the identical K=2560 dot product, so logits should stay within the 0.02 atol/rtol gates and greedy tokens identical; the measured risk is a cuBLAS kernel/accumulation-order change at N=19456 perturbing bf16 results by ~1 ulp, watched by the exact-greedy-token and logits checks. Each replacement is signature-guarded (same in_features 2560, BF16, cuda, no extra args/kwargs) and falls back to the parent's original bound forward on any mismatch, on weight mutation (identity + version-counter checks against the build-time snapshot), or on any exception, so incompatible invocations keep exact parent semantics. Eliminated calls (288 IDs = selected groups a6aa67ffe84fe2f7c9de, 0c566a3a363f294c6750, bd1a5d5adecd8a00db28, b2cb73f1b7a24f0e6d21): the per-layer gate_proj/up_proj nn.Linear module calls and their aten::linear functional twins no longer execute because the packed GEMM inside the MLP replacement subsumes both dot products with the same operands; their sole consumer is the arithmetic inside the same replaced MLP forward, which now computes those products itself, so downstream consumers (SiLU/mul input, down_proj input) receive the same values. down_proj and act_fn keep running through their original submodule objects, so their observed call sites (aten::silu, aten::mul, down_proj module call and its aten::linear) still execute with the same shapes; only their gate operand arrives as a stride-19456 view instead of a contiguous tensor, an accounting stride change the recaptured plan will observe, not a value change. The opop::NNN profiler._record_function children listed in affected_calls are discovery instrumentation around the removed inner dispatches, not semantic workload calls; they disappear together with the eliminated linears and have no consumers in the measured path. Replacements are mutually compatible: prefill and decode sites of the same module share one closure, so installation order cannot change behavior; no installed bundles exist to replace (search.json installed_bundles is empty) and no fixture-dependent outputs are cached - the full workload executes on every invocation. No inputs/previous-feedback.txt is present, so this attempt is derived from the frozen selection hypothesis and the observed diagnostics only.
proposal.setup_work: At build time (once, after prepare, before validation; outside the timed workload boundary) each of the 36 Qwen3MLP modules contributes one torch.cat of its frozen gate_proj.weight and up_proj.weight ([9728,2560] + [9728,2560] BF16) into a packed [19456,2560] BF16 weight held in the replacement closure. Extra GPU memory: 36 x 19456 x 2560 x 2 B = 3,586,129,920 B ~= 3.34 GiB (95 MiB per layer) resident for the warm-model lifetime, in addition to the untouched original parameters (~3.34 GiB gate+up); build cost is 36 small device copies (well under a second) plus closure setup, no kernels run per call beyond the packed GEMM itself. Valid for this task's warm-model lifecycle: the adapter loads weights once in prepare and reset() never mutates them (seed/eval/sync only), so the packed snapshot is invariant; the replacement re-validates weight identity and version counters on every call and falls back to the parent forward if the snapshot could ever be stale. Same closure object is returned for the prefill and decode call sites of a module; parameters dict is unused because no tunable parameters are declared.
proposal.quality_risks: bf16 GEMM kernel selection for N=19456 may differ from N=9728 (tile shape, split-K), changing fp32 accumulation order; expected perturbation is ~1 ulp in bf16 and must stay inside logits atol/rtol 0.02, but require_exact_greedy_tokens could fail if the top-2 logits of any step are tied within that margin - this is the primary measured risk and is tested by the paired quality gates, not assumed away. SilU/mul now read strided views (row stride 19456 instead of 9728) of the packed projection; values are identical and cost is negligible at these sizes, but observed child-call strides change, which affects plan recapture accounting only. If weights were mutated after build (not the case in this adapter), the identity/version guards trigger a fallback to the original parent forward, restoring exact baseline behavior at baseline speed. If build ran under inference_mode, the packed tensor is materialized with inference mode locally disabled so it stays usable in both inference and grad-enabled callers; if cat were to fail for any reason the fallback path again yields parent semantics. No training, gradients or parameter updates exist in this workload (adapter run is @torch.inference_mode, model.eval()); the packed weight is built with autograd connectivity from the original parameters so even a hypothetical grad-enabled caller computes the same math, but optimizer step compatibility was not exercised because no optimizer exists here.

external_invariants: Model is pretrained Qwen3-4B loaded from the local asset snapshot with dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation='sdpa', local_files_only=True, in eval mode on context['device'].
Numerical policy matches common.configure(): torch.manual_seed(20261020), matmul/cudnn TF32 disabled, cudnn.benchmark disabled, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', 4 CPU threads, 1 interop thread.
Input is real data: the chat-templated source prompt encoded without special tokens, tiled and truncated to exactly 256 prompt tokens, replicated across batch=1, resident on GPU.
Decoding is greedy argmax over the last-position logits; no sampling, temperature, EOS stopping, or early exit; exactly 32 tokens are generated.
Every forward uses use_cache=True with a KV cache created fresh per run; decode steps feed exactly one token; logits_to_keep=1 as in the source.
ttft boundary is the source's explicit torch.cuda.synchronize() immediately after the first forward/argmax; the workload boundary is the final torch.cuda.synchronize() after the last decode step.
The full workload (prefill plus all 31 decode steps) always executes, in every mode, even though the objective measures only the first-token phase.
Quality comparison uses the source tolerances (atol=rtol=0.02 on logits) and exact greedy token equality; no accuracy or convergence beyond reference fidelity is claimed.
No CUDA initialization or model loading at import time; no second reference model is allocated on GPU; the process group (none here, single process) is never destroyed.
